reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g2_na_q3_0), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample questions directly fulfill the competency requirement of counting objects in groups using repeated addition and equal grouping concepts. For example, questions like "There are 4 groups of 3 (3 + 3 + 3 + 3). How many in all?" and "Shade 3 groups of 2 squares to show 2 + 2 + 2. How many squares did you shade in all?" explicitly connect the group structure to the corresponding repeated addition sentence.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items comprehensively cover multiple representations including array models in "Look at the array. It shows 3 groups of 3 (3 + 3 + 3). How many squares are shaded in all?", concrete shading tasks in "Shade 2 groups of 5 squares to show 5 + 5. How many squares did you shade in all?", real-world groupings in "Moses puts 2 baskets in each of 5 bags. How many baskets are in all the bags?", and repeated addition equivalence in "There are 2 groups of 5. By repeated addition, 5 + 5 = 10. True or False?".

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The linguistic and cognitive demands are well-calibrated for Grade 2 Quarter 3 students. Sentences are concise and scaffolded with clear repeated addition expressions, as seen in "3 groups of 2 (2 + 2 + 2) makes ___ in all" and "There are 2 groups of 3 (3 + 3). How many in all?", avoiding overly complex phrasing while building foundational multiplication readiness.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: A wide spectrum of problem formats is utilized, including standard MCQ, cloze fill-ins, visual array reading, shading manipulatives, error detection, and true/false validation. Representative items include "Look at the array. It shows 4 groups of 2 (2 + 2 + 2 + 2). How many squares are shaded in all?", "Shade 7 groups of 10 squares to show 10 added 7 times. How many squares did you shade in all?", and error detection (seed 51: "5 + 5").

competency_alignment.rationale: All sampled items strictly align with the MATATAG learning competency without introducing advanced multiplication algorithms or extraneous arithmetic operations. Each problem reinforces the link between equal groups and repeated addition, such as "There are 5 groups of 2 (2 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 2). How many in all?" and "2 groups of 4 (4 + 4) makes ___ in all".

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical scale is completely appropriate for Grade 2, spanning small group sums like "There are 2 groups of 2 (2 + 2). How many in all?" up to upper-boundary sums within 100 such as "There are 10 groups of 8 (8 added 10 times). How many in all?" and "There are 10 groups of 10. By repeated addition, 10 added 10 times = 100. True or False?".
